## Slides are level-2 headings

Each `##` starts a new slide.

-   A `#` heading becomes a full-screen section divider.

-   `. . .` reveals the content after it on a click.

. . .

Like this.

## Two columns

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Left-hand content.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Right-hand content.
:::
::::

## Branded content boxes

::: {.content-box-marine}
`.content-box-marine` — for the point you want the room to remember.
:::

::: {.content-box-oil}
`.content-box-oil` — for supporting detail.
:::

## A background image

Set it on the slide heading:

``` markdown
## {background-image="img/figure.png" background-size="cover"}
```

## Code

```{r}
#| echo: true
1 + 1
```

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes go in a `.notes` div and are visible in speaker view (press `s`).
:::

## Using this theme as a Quarto theme instead

`css:` layers plain CSS over the stock theme, which is enough for most
decks and works straight from the URL above.

For full control — fonts, heading colours, the title slide — vendor a
copy of [`exts-reveal.scss`](/themes/exts-reveal.scss) next to your deck
and use `theme:` instead. Quarto does not resolve `theme:` over http, so
it has to be a local file:

``` yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: [default, exts-reveal.scss]
```
